# Configure event sinks

Boundary emits audit, observation, system, and telemetry events and writes them to the sinks you configure. This page describes how to configure the `events` stanza, add a stderr sink and a file sink, send events to multiple sinks, and control how audit events handle sensitive data.

## Requirements

- Access to the Boundary configuration file of the controller or worker you want to configure.
- For a file sink, a directory that exists and is writable by the Boundary service user.

## Default configuration

If the configuration file has no `events` stanza, Boundary uses the following default. If you define an `events` stanza with no `sink` blocks, Boundary also uses this default stderr sink.

```hcl
events {
  audit_enabled        = false
  observations_enabled = true
  sysevents_enabled    = true
  telemetry_enabled    = false
  sink "stderr" {
    name        = "default"
    event_types = ["*"]
    format      = "cloudevents-json"
  }
}
```

You can define the `events` stanza only once in a configuration file.

## Enable event types

Use the following parameters in the `events` stanza to control which event types Boundary emits:

- `audit_enabled` emits audit events.
- `observations_enabled` emits observation events.
- `sysevents_enabled` emits system events.
- `telemetry_enabled` emits telemetry events. You must also set `observations_enabled = true` to receive telemetry events.

A sink only receives the event types listed in its `event_types` parameter. Enable each type in the stanza and list it in at least one sink.

## Configure a stderr sink

The stderr sink writes events to standard error. It is useful in containerized deployments where a log collector reads from stdout and stderr.

1. Open the Boundary configuration file.
1. Add a `sink` block with the `stderr` label inside the `events` stanza.

   ```hcl
   events {
     observations_enabled = true
     sysevents_enabled    = true
     sink "stderr" {
       name        = "all-events"
       description = "All events sent to stderr"
       event_types = ["*"]
       format      = "hclog-text"
     }
   }
   ```

1. Restart Boundary.

The stderr sink supports only the [common sink parameters](/boundary/docs/monitor/events/common).

## Configure a file sink

The file sink writes events to a local file and supports rotation by size, duration, or file count.

### Create the log directory

Create the log directory before starting Boundary and give the Boundary service user write access.

```shell-session
$ sudo mkdir -p /var/log/boundary
$ sudo chown boundary:boundary /var/log/boundary
$ sudo chmod 750 /var/log/boundary
```

Replace `boundary:boundary` with the user and group that run the Boundary service. For more information, refer to [Set logging permissions](/boundary/tutorials/enterprise/ent-deployment-guide#set-logging-permissions).

### Add the file sink

1. Open the Boundary configuration file.
1. Add a `sink` block with a nested `file` block inside the `events` stanza.

   ```hcl
   events {
     observations_enabled = true
     sysevents_enabled    = true
     sink {
       name        = "obs-sink"
       description = "Observations sent to a file"
       event_types = ["observation"]
       format      = "cloudevents-json"
       file {
         path      = "/var/log/boundary"
         file_name = "events.ndjson"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

1. Restart Boundary.

### Rotate the file

To rotate the file, add rotation parameters to the `file` block. The following example rotates the file every 24 hours or when it reaches 10 MB, and keeps five rotated files.

```hcl
file {
  path             = "/var/log/boundary"
  file_name        = "events.ndjson"
  rotate_bytes     = 10000000
  rotate_duration  = "24h"
  rotate_max_files = 5
}
```

For all `file` parameters, refer to [File sink parameters](/boundary/docs/monitor/events/file).

## Send events to multiple sinks

You can define the `sink` block more than once to send events to multiple destinations. Each file sink must have a unique combination of `path` and `file_name`.

```hcl
events {
  observations_enabled = true
  sysevents_enabled    = true
  sink "stderr" {
    name        = "all-events"
    description = "All events sent to stderr"
    event_types = ["*"]
    format      = "hclog-text"
  }
  sink {
    name        = "obs-sink"
    description = "Observations sent to a file"
    event_types = ["observation"]
    format      = "cloudevents-json"
    file {
      path      = "/var/log/boundary"
      file_name = "events.ndjson"
    }
  }
}
```

To control which events each sink receives, add `allow_filters` or `deny_filters`. Refer to [Filter events](/boundary/docs/monitor/events/filter-events).

## Configure audit event handling

Audit events can contain data that Boundary classifies as sensitive or secret. The `audit_config` block in a sink controls how Boundary processes those fields. Boundary ignores `audit_config` if the sink does not receive `audit` events.

Set `audit_enabled = true` in the `events` stanza and include `audit` or `*` in the sink's `event_types` to receive audit events.

By default, Boundary redacts both sensitive and secret fields. The following example shows the default settings explicitly:

```hcl
audit_config {
  audit_filter_overrides {
    sensitive = "redact"
    secret    = "redact"
  }
}
```

To apply an HMAC to sensitive fields and encrypt secret fields:

```hcl
audit_config {
  audit_filter_overrides {
    sensitive = "hmac-sha256"
    secret    = "encrypt"
  }
}
```

To include sensitive fields such as email addresses and usernames without a filter, set `sensitive` to an empty string. The empty string overrides the default redaction.

```hcl
audit_config {
  audit_filter_overrides {
    sensitive = ""
  }
}
```
